One place where people learn together

Brain health does not sit in one profession. A person with a stroke needs a doctor, a therapist, a pharmacist, a nurse and a family that understands. A child with a language difficulty needs a teacher, a speech-language therapist and a parent who knows what to do. NeuroSphere is building one place where these people learn together, where families find their way, and where Pakistan's own data guides what we do.
Our journey for every person: Understand. Protect. Treat. Rebuild. Learn. Discover.
We start with teaching and public education. Clinical navigation, research and the physical hub follow, each opening only when it is ready and approved.

A young population of about 260 million, with a median age of about 20.6 years. Source: Worldometer (UN-based estimate), October 2026.

SECTION: GUIDE: STROKE, KNOW THE SIGNS AND ACT FAST
A stroke happens when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked, or when a blood vessel in the brain bleeds. Treatment works best when it starts early.
Sudden drooping of the face or an uneven smile.
Weakness or numbness in an arm or leg, often on one side.
Sudden loss of vision or balance.
What to do: call emergency services at once and note the time the signs began. Do not give food, drink or medicine by mouth. Keep the person safe and comfortable while help arrives.
After a stroke, rehabilitation with a team of professionals, including doctors, nurses, therapists and a pharmacist, helps recovery, and families have an important part to play.

SECTION: GUIDE: EPILEPSY, SEIZURE FIRST AID

Epilepsy is a condition in which the brain has repeated seizures. Most seizures stop on their own within a few minutes. Epilepsy is not contagious, and people with epilepsy can live full lives with the right care.
If someone has a seizure with shaking:
Stay calm and note the time.
Move hard or sharp objects away and cushion the head.
Do not hold the person down and do not put anything in their mouth.
When the shaking stops, gently turn the person onto their side.
Stay until they are fully alert and speak calmly to them.
Call emergency services if the seizure lasts more than five minutes, if another seizure follows, if the person is injured, or if they do not wake up.

About NeuroSphere | Our mission, roadmap and governance
Why NeuroSphere exists, how we work, who guides us and how we are growing.

Pakistan has a young, fast-growing population and too few trained specialists in neurology, mental health, rehabilitation and genetics. Many families travel long distances, and many young health graduates cannot find structured training or supervised research. NeuroSphere began from a simple idea: bring together people who care about the brain, and train and connect them, step by step.

A Pakistan in which every person, from a child in school to an older adult at home, can understand, protect and, when needed, restore their brain health, supported by trustworthy science and local expertise.

To build a complete brain-health institution that turns research into everyday practice: informing the public, guiding patients and families to the right care, training clinicians and students, producing Pakistani evidence, and working with hospitals, universities and policymakers.
Honesty. We say what is known and not known. We never promise cures.
Patient and public first, in Urdu and English.
Scientific integrity: real data, ethics approval and fair authorship.
Equity: reaching beyond big cities and wealthy households.
Accountability: clear governance, public reporting and privacy.
Collaboration: we connect hospitals and universities; we do not compete with them.
